lesson.content:
## What it is
A network is a set of devices (nodes) connected by communication links so they can share data and resources. [p. 1]
## Real-life analogy
Imagine a school where students can share their notes and resources with each other. Each student is a node, and the shared resources are the data. [p. 1]
## How it works
1. Devices are connected by communication links, such as cables or wireless signals. [p. 1]
2. Data is transmitted from one device to another through these links. [p. 1]
## Key terms
- **PAN (Personal Area Network)**: Devices around one person, e.g. Bluetooth earphones, range of a few metres. [p. 1]
- **LAN (Local Area Network)**: One building or campus, high speed, owned privately. [p. 1]
- **MAN (Metropolitan Area Network)**: A city, e.g. a cable TV network. [p. 1]
- **WAN (Wide Area Network)**: A country or the world; the Internet is the largest WAN. [p. 1]
## Example
A small example of a LAN could be a network connecting computers in a single office building. [p. 1]
## What to draw in the exam
No diagram needed. [p. 1]
## Exam tip
Identify the type of network in a scenario and explain its characteristics. [p. 1]
